stories.headline: Supreme Court refuses to entertain PIL on recurring Assam floods
stories.title: Supreme Court refuses to entertain PIL on recurring Assam floods
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi, Oct 5: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to entertain a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking directions to ensure effective measures to prevent recurring floods, riverbank erosion and drainage-related problems in Assam and the Brahmaputra Valley.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, while declining to entertain the plea filed by advocate Ujjawal Gaur, directed the registry to forward a copy of the petition to all the respondent authorities, asking them to look into the issues raised and take appropriate remedial measures.
Appearing in person, Gaur submitted that the administrative lapses highlighted in the petition were amenable to judicial scrutiny and urged the apex court to issue notice to the authorities.

However, the CJI-led Bench observed that the various suggestions and deficiencies highlighted by the petitioner ought to draw the attention of the concerned authorities, but the issue was "not essentially legal" in nature.
Declining to entertain the PIL, the top court directed its registry to forward the petition to all the respondents, who would look into its contents and take appropriate remedial measures.

The plea had sought judicial intervention to ensure effective implementation of the statutory framework governing flood and erosion management and had proposed, among other measures, a high-level expert mechanism to examine the recurring problems.

The petitioner had contended that the recurring devastation caused by floods could not be treated as wholly inevitable when statutory frameworks and specialised institutions had been created for flood control, bank erosion and drainage management.

The plea referred to the Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980, the Assam Embankment and Drainage Act, 1953 and the River Boards Act, 1956, arguing that these laws contemplated scientific investigation, integrated river-basin planning and implementation of measures relating to floods, erosion and drainage.

It relied on successive reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) which, according to the petitioner, had recorded deficiencies in flood-control planning, execution and maintenance, drainage management, floodplain management and monitoring of projects.

stories.headline: CEC & Election Commissioners Enjoy Greater Legal Immunity Than Even Judges, Remarks Supreme Court
stories.title: CEC & Election Commissioners Enjoy Greater Legal Immunity Than Even Judges, Remarks Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5) orally observed that the legal protection granted to the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners under the 2023 law may be broader than the protection available even to constitutional court judges, during the hearing of petitions challenging the decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by CEC Gyanesh Kumar in connection with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing the petitions.

Senior Advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, argued that the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners(Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, had substantially enhanced the authority and immunity of the CEC and Election Commissioners.
As per Section 16 of the 2023 Act, CEC and Election Commissioners are protected from civil or criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge or purported discharge of their official functions.
The legal protection continues even after they have demitted office.
At this stage, Justice Bagchi made a significant observation regarding the extent of the protection.
"This protection is perhaps only for the President.
It does not apply even to judges," Justice Bagchi observed.
Singh agreed with the observation and argued that the statutory scheme had placed the CEC in a position of extraordinary legal protection.
"Even the Prime Minister does not have this," Singh submitted.
He argued that the statutory framework had effectively placed the CEC "on a pedestal even higher than Supreme Court judges."
"ECI more powerful today than any other constitutional authority," Singh submitted.

stories.headline: Spain heads to early election on November 29 as Sánchez government faces setbacks
stories.title: Spain heads to early election on November 29 as Sánchez government faces setbacks
stories.summary: The prime minister’s announcement follows consultations with ministers and PSOE members after his government struggled to advance its legislative agenda
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called an early general election for November 29 after his government suffered a parliamentary defeat over two housing measures, amid mounting political pressure, a worsening housing crisis, migration challenges and corruption cases involving figures close to his Socialist Party (PSOE), Euronews reported.

According to Euronews, the announcement follows a weekend of consultations by Sánchez with ministers and senior members of the PSOE, as the prime minister weighed whether to continue governing until the end of the parliamentary term or seek a fresh mandate.
The decision came after Spain’s lower house rejected two government-backed housing decrees on Friday.
Despite last-minute negotiations aimed at securing sufficient parliamentary support, the measures failed to pass, Euronews reported.
The defeated decrees formed part of the government’s response to Spain’s growing housing crisis, which has emerged as a key political challenge for Sánchez’s administration.

The prime minister’s decision also comes against the backdrop of increasing pressure on his coalition government, which has struggled to maintain support in the Spanish Congress because of its fragile parliamentary majority.

The government has been forced to negotiate its legislative agenda on a vote-by-vote basis with its parliamentary partners and has suffered several defeats in Congress, making it increasingly difficult to advance its policies, as reported by Euronews.
At the same time, a migration crisis in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta has added to the political strain.
At the end of July, tens of thousands of migrants crossed the border from Morocco, placing unprecedented pressure on the enclave in North Africa.
The Spanish government subsequently deployed additional resources and, weeks later, declared a “situation of interest for national security” for the first time in Spain’s democratic era.
The government’s handling of the situation has triggered criticism from the opposition.
The conservative People’s Party (PP) and far-right Vox have accused the government of responding too slowly and have questioned its policy towards Morocco, Euronews reported.

stories.headline: PDP holds Lal Chowk Zonal Committee election
stories.title: PDP holds Lal Chowk Zonal Committee election
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 5: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Lal Chowk Constituency, Monday held elections for its Zonal Committee at the party office in Lal Chowk. The proceedings, as per a statement, were presided over by Zahoor Ahmad Mir, former MLA and Cabinet Minister. Following the voting process, Reyaz Ahmad Dar was elected as the Zonal President. The election proceedings were attended by Zuhaib Yousf Mir, In-Charge Lal Chowk Constituency; PDP Spokesperson Iqbal Tramboo; former State Secretary Arif Laigaroo; former State Secretary Abdul Hameed Koshen; and Abdul Qayoom Bhat. Speaking on the occasion, Zuhaib Yousf Mir emphasised the importance of strengthening the party organisation at the grassroots and said that organisational elections must go beyond the mere appointment of office-bearers. “These elections should mean more than merely choosing office-bearers. They should help strengthen the party at the grassroots, deepen our engagement with people and give greater meaning and responsibility to our organisational structure. The real significance of these elections will lie in how effectively we translate this organisational exercise into stronger engagement with the people,” Mir said.

stories.headline: Deliver on election promises, address public issues: Ravinder Raina
stories.title: Deliver on election promises, address public issues: Ravinder Raina
stories.summary: Kupwara, Oct 5: Former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Jammu and Kashmir UT President and senior leader Ravinder Raina Monday said, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah should focus on addressing the issues confronting the people of Jammu and Kashmir instead of repeatedly taking refuge in the demand for restoration of statehood. Speaking to reporters in Kupwara before he left for Seemari Karnah, Raina said the Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi has already assured that statehood would be restored to Jammu and Kashmir, adding that the process was being pursued while security-related concerns were also being taken into consideration. "Statehood should be restored at the earliest but certain security concerns also need to be taken into account. The matter is being addressed at the appropriate level," Raina said. Taking a dig at Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Raina said Omar Abdullah was an elected representative and should concentrate on fulfilling the commitments made to the people. "Instead of seeking refuge in the statehood issue, the Chief Minister should address the grievances of the people and work for development," he added. "There was no need for Omar Abdullah to resign, instead he should use his tenure to deliver on the promises made to the people in his party’s election manifesto," he added. On the security situation, Raina claimed that Jammu and Kashmir was witnessing a peaceful environment, adding that stone-pelting and shutdowns have ended which was a positive sign with regard development. Reacting to recent remarks by National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on mistakes committed by the Congress and former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, Raina said the statement vindicated the BJP’s position maintained over the years. "When a senior leader like Farooq Abdullah acknowledges that mistakes were committed by the Congress and Jawaharlal Nehru, it validates what the BJP has been saying all these years," he added. Raina called for peace, harmony and brotherhood among people. BJP leader Javed Qureshi and other party workers were also present on the occasion.

stories.headline: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down from India women's team captaincy
stories.title: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down from India women's team captaincy
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 06: Indian women's cricket team's long-serving captain Harmanpreet Kaur on Tuesday stepped down from her position in all three formats, saying that she has done her duty as leader and is now "ready to play for the love of the game again." Harmanpreet's announcement came after a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati to evaluate the team's trajectory in the past few months. Chaired by BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, the meeting was attended by Harmanpreet, vice-captain Smriti Mandhana and head coach Amol Muzumdar. The 37-year-old led the Indian T20 side for a decade, taking over the position in 2016, and was elevated to ODI captaincy in 2022 before becoming the all-format leader in 2023. "Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women's Cricket Team across all formats," she posted on her instagram account. "This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life," Harmanpreet said in a lengthy statement. "Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues," she added. Harmanpreet, under whom India won its maiden ODI World Cup in November last year and recently picked up a second successive Asian Games gold in the T20 format, said she is leaving the captaincy "with a heart full of emotions, but also with peace." "Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place," she said.

stories.title: Three new Supreme Court judges to take oath at 3.30 pm, departure from usual morning practice
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant will administer the oath to newly appointed Supreme Court judges Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Aparesh Kumar Singh at 3:30 p.m., marking a departure from the court’s usual morning swearing-in tradition.

article_sentences: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant will administer the oath to newly appointed Supreme Court judges Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Aparesh Kumar Singh at 3:30 p.m., marking a departure from the court’s usual morning swearing-in tradition.

New Delhi: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant will on Tuesday administer the oath of office to three new judges of the Supreme Court -- Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh -- at 3.30 p.m. The swearing-in ceremony, which will be live-streamed, marks a departure from the usual practice of administering the oath to newly appointed Supreme Court judges in the morning.
Newly appointed Supreme Court judges usually take the oath of office at 10.30 a.m., coinciding with the time when the top court assembles on working days to conduct hearings.

However, according to an official communication issued in this regard, “The Swearing-in-Ceremony of Justice Sunita Agarwal, Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, shall be live-streamed from 03:30 P.M. onwards.”
The three Chief Justices of the High Courts were appointed as judges of the apex court after the Centre cleared their elevation on the recommendation of the Supreme Court Collegium.
Acting swiftly on the Collegium's recommendation, the Centre on Monday approved the elevation of Justices Agarwal, Upadhyaya and Singh to the Supreme Court.

In a post on X, Union Minister for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal announced that the President, after consultation with CJI Surya Kant, had appointed the three Chief Justices as judges of the apex court.

“The Supreme Court Collegium in its meeting held on 28th September, 2026 has recommended elevation of the following Chief Justices of the High Courts as Judges in the Supreme Court,” the Collegium had said in a statement uploaded on the apex court's official website.
Justice Agarwal, born on April 30, 1966, was appointed as a judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011.
She became the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court on July 23, 2023.
Justice Upadhyaya, born on June 16, 1965, was appointed as a puisne Judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011 and became a permanent Judge on August 6, 2013.
He became the Senior Judge of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on March 28, 2023.

stories.headline: Chief Justice Bhatti felicitated by Srinagar Bar Association
stories.title: Chief Justice Bhatti felicitated by Srinagar Bar Association
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 5: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court Bar Association Srinagar on Monday organised a felicitation programme in honour of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhatti at the Common Bar Room of the Srinagar Wing of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. Judges of the High Court, including Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal, Justice Rajesh Sekhri, Justice Mohammad Yousuf Wani, Justice Sanjay Parihar and newly appointed Justice Yashpal Bourney, besides Judicial Member and HoD, Central Administrative Tribunal, Srinagar, Mir Syed Lateef, attended the function. The judges were also felicitated. President of the Bar Association, Waseem Gul, delivered the welcome address, while Advocate Bikram Deep Singh conducted the proceedings. A large number of advocates attended the event, including senior advocates Zaffar Ahmad Shah, G A Lone, R A Jan, Mohsin Ul Showkat Qadri, Syed Faisal Qadri, Tahir Majid Shamsi, Anupam Raina, Jehangir Ganie, Syed Manzoor, Anil Bhan, Bashir Ahmad Bashir, Showkat Makroo, Abdul Majid Dar, Arifa Jan and Masooda Jan, besides other lawyers and law officers. ‘Strong Bar essential for good judgments’ Responding to the felicitation, Chief Justice Bhatti expressed appreciation for the warmth extended by the Bar and recalled his 24-25 years as a lawyer. He paid tribute to senior members of the legal fraternity and said his association with the Bar had given him a deep understanding of the profession and its responsibilities. The Chief Justice said he had come to recognise nearly 90 percent of the faces in the Bar, describing the familiarity as a source of professional satisfaction. He sought the cooperation of lawyers in protecting the constitutional rights of citizens within the framework of law.

body: The judges were also felicitated.
President of the Bar Association, Waseem Gul, delivered the welcome address, while Advocate Bikram Deep Singh conducted the proceedings.

A large number of advocates attended the event, including senior advocates Zaffar Ahmad Shah, G. A Lone, R A Jan, Mohsin Ul Showkat Qadri, Syed Faisal Qadri, Tahir Majid Shamsi, Anupam Raina, Jehangir Ganie, Syed Manzoor, Anil Bhan, Bashir Ahmad Bashir, Showkat Makroo, Abdul Majid Dar, Arifa Jan and Masooda Jan, besides other lawyers and law officers.
‘Strong Bar essential for good judgments’ Responding to the felicitation, Chief Justice Bhatti expressed appreciation for the warmth extended by the Bar and recalled his 24-25 years as a lawyer.
He paid tribute to senior members of the legal fraternity and said his association with the Bar had given him a deep understanding of the profession and its responsibilities.
The Chief Justice said he had come to recognise nearly 90 percent of the faces in the Bar, describing the familiarity as a source of professional satisfaction.
He sought the cooperation of lawyers in protecting the constitutional rights of citizens within the framework of law.

stories.headline: Supreme Court 7-Judge Bench Disposes Reference On Legislative Privilege As Infructuous
stories.title: Supreme Court 7-Judge Bench Disposes Reference On Legislative Privilege As Infructuous
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today closed the 7-judge reference on the issue of legislative privileges vis-a-vis free speech, noting that the 2003 resolution of the Tamil Nadu legislative assembly, which was the trigger for the case, was withdrawn in 2004.

A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Aravind Kumar, Justice PK Mishra, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice Vipul Pancholi, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Justice V Mohana was constituted to hear the matter, which had been pending for nearly 2 decades.
Today, while disposing of the matter as infructuous, the bench noted that the withdrawal of the impugned resolution skipped the notice of the Court while passing the reference order.
The bench observed that the cause of action for the reference has become infructuous, and closed the matter.
However, the bench left the questions of law open for adjudication in an appropriate case.
After the order was dictated, Senior Advocate AM Singhvi commented in a lighter vein that the Court has set two records - shortest hearing and quickest disposal of a 7-judge matter.
Yesterday, on mentioning of the matter, CJI Surya Kant had expressed that the reference might be disposed of as an academic issue.
The reference originated from the 2003 case N. Ravi.
Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai, challenging the 2003 decision taken by the Tamil Nadu assembly to sentence 5 journalists of The Hindu for articles criticizing the State Government.
The matter was ultimately referred to the 7-judge bench to examine the interplay between Articles 194(3), 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution.
The reference remained pending for over two decades, and the Court, in August 2026, decided to commence the hearing from October 6.
Yesterday, Senior Advocate Raju Ramachandran, for the State of Tamil Nadu, informed a 3-judge bench led by CJI Surya Kant that the 2003 resolution of the Assembly was revoked in 2004 itself.

stories.title: Punjab Govt Moves Supreme Court Against HC Order For CBI Probe Into Corruption Allegations Linked To Chief Minister's Office
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Punjab government has moved the Supreme Court challenging the Punjab and Haryana High Court's order directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to register a criminal case and probe allegations of corruption linked to the office of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.
The Special Leave Petition (SLP) was filed by the State government, challenging the order passed by the High Court on Monday.

A High Court bench comprising Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor had on Monday directed the CBI to register a criminal case into allegations concerning Rajbir Singh Ghuman, Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann.
The High Court further directed the State of Punjab and the Punjab.
Police to provide all assistance to the CBI for conducting a fair investigation.
The directions were passed while hearing a Public Interest Litigation filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf.
The PIL alleged that the Punjab.
Police had failed to take appropriate action despite communications from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) seeking a probe into allegations against Ghuman.

According to the submissions before the High Court, the ED had flagged allegations involving one Nitin Gohal, who allegedly acted as an intermediary for persons seeking various favours from the Punjab government.
The allegations relate, among other things, to facilitating transfers, providing access to confidential government documents, facilitating arms licences and securing other benefits.
The High Court, after considering the material placed before it, directed the CBI to register a criminal case and investigate the allegations.
The Punjab government's challenge before the Supreme Court seeks to overturn the High Court's direction for a CBI investigation.

stories.title: Supreme Court Denies Approval of Modified Form 6, Seeks Clarification on Changes
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday made it clear that it had not approved any modified version of Form 6, used for enrolling new voters in electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant made the observation while hearing a plea seeking suspension and prosecution of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
"Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us.
Let's be clear.
When the record is produced, we would like to see who has modified," Kant observed during the hearing.
Earlier, in a press statement issued on September 26 after a key meeting, the Election Commission had said, "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used."
A key grievance concerns the alteration of Form 6 during SIR of electoral rolls.

Commissioner Joshi had allegedly objected that the form could not be changed to require SIR-linked disclosures without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, an objection subsequently endorsed by Sandhu.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Declines Interim Suspension of CEC, Seeks Responses from Centre and ECI
stories.title: Supreme Court Declines Interim Suspension of CEC, Seeks Responses from Centre and ECI
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass an ex-parte interim order seeking suspension of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations that key decisions relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken unilaterally, saying the Election Commission and others must first be heard.

A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also issued notices to the Centre, Election Commission of India (ECI), CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg and DG (IT) Seema Khanna.
"Let's first have authenticated information on that.
We can always annul any decision…," observed the bench.
The petition relied on a report claiming that 14 crucial SIR-related decisions were taken in the name of the ECI despite objections recorded by the two other Election Commissioners.

Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for one of the petitioners, Rakesh Kumar Singh, sought immediate suspension of the CEC, contending that the alleged unilateral decisions posed a serious threat to electoral democracy.
Referring to Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, Singh submitted that ECI decisions were required to be unanimous or, failing that, taken by majority.
As Singh sought suspension of the CEC, the bench questioned the feasibility of suspending the CEC, observing that it could stall the functioning of the poll panel.
"Who will conduct the elections?" the bench asked.
Singh responded that the other two.
Election Commissioners could discharge the functions.
The bench said it would have to first examine the allegations after receiving responses from the respondents.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Denies Bail to Shyamkanu Mahanta in Zubeen Garg Death Case
stories.title: Supreme Court Denies Bail to Shyamkanu Mahanta in Zubeen Garg Death Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Guwahati: In a major setback, Shyamkanu Mahanta, one of the accused in the Zubeen Garg death case and currently lodged at Baksa District Jail, didn't get relief from the Supreme Court (SC) on Monday.
The apex court refused to issue a ruling on his bail plea and instead fixed November 4 as the next date for hearing.
Speaking to the media, Assam's advocate general Devajit Lon Saikia said this was the third hearing of Mahanta's bail plea.
He also mentioned that out of the 10 witnesses from Singapore in the case, the fast track court had examined the testimonies of eight.
He said the SC had been informed that testimonies of the remaining two witnesses from Singapore would be completed by October 12.
According to him, the SC fixed November 4 as the next date for hearing of Mahanta's bail plea "after hearing our argument".
He said the apex court had also been informed that trial was continuing in the fast track court on a day-to-day basis.
Noting that there were total 394 witnesses, Saikia was of the opinion that the testimony of all might not be required, "but we will examine some for material witness".
Meanwhile, commenting on the status of the Zubeen's death case in the fast track court, special public prosecutor.
Ziaul Kamar said trial proceedings were continuing in a speedy manner.
He revealed that 122 prosecution witnesses had been examined so far, including nine non-resident Indians (NRIs) in the past 70-80 working days.
Altogether 86 FIRs were filed at various police stations across the state following the sudden and mysterious death of Assam's cultural icon Zubeen Garg in Singapore in September last year.

stories.headline: Centre elevates three Chief Justices to Supreme Court
stories.title: Centre elevates three Chief Justices to Supreme Court
stories.summary: With fresh appointments, working strength of the apex court rises to 37
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Centre on Monday (October 5, 2026) appointed the Chief Justices of the Gujarat, Delhi, and Telangana High Courts to the Supreme Court.
The three additional judges will take the court’s working strength to 37, leaving one vacancy against its sanctioned strength of 38.

Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said on X that Justice Sunita Agarwal, Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court; Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court; and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court have been appointed to the SC.
Justice Sunita Agarwal is originally from the Allahabad High Court and has served as Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court for around 3 years since July 2023.
She will retire from the Supreme Court in April 2031.
Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, who became a judge in 2011 after serving as Uttar Pradesh’s Chief Standing Counsel, was appointed Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court in July 2023.
He was transferred to the Delhi High Court in January 2025.
Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh had practised before the Patna and Jharkhand High Courts before becoming a judge in 2012.
He served as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court before taking charge as Telangana High Court Chief Justice in July 2025.
They are set to be sworn in on October 6.
The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended their elevation on September 28.

stories.headline: IMD: Heavy rain likely over TN, Kerala, Mahe, Puducherry, Karnataka in coming days
stories.title: IMD: Heavy rain likely over TN, Kerala, Mahe, Puducherry, Karnataka in coming days
stories.summary: Bay of Bengal expected to swing to easterlies as an approaching wave sets up the transition; north-east monsoon could arrive in next 10 days around normal time, suggest models
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Withdrawal of south-west monsoon briefly stalled on Monday over Central and East India, with the retreating edge stretching in an arc through Supaul; Ranchi; Raipur; Brahmapuri; Parbhani; Baramati and Harnai, and the western end nestling in Maharashtra.
Farther south, the atmosphere is preparing for the next seasonal act.
Winds over the South Peninsula are showing a growing inclination to turn from south-westerly to easterly, the defining signal of the transition to the north-east monsoon.
Easterlies have established themselves over the Arabian Sea, and the adjoining South Peninsula is expected to follow suit shortly.
The missing piece is the Bay of Bengal, where the wind regime must turn decisively before the north-east monsoon can properly take hold.
The normal window for this transition opens around October 15.
Forecast models suggest the seasonal reversal could unfold broadly on schedule this year, with an easterly wave moving in from the South China Sea providing the initial trigger.

It could set up a cyclonic circulation over the Andaman Sea before moving into the central Bay of Bengal, past the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, around October 14, and draw north-easterlies towards the South Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu coasts, strengthening the seasonally reversing flows.
The atmospheric stage was already being set on Monday evening.
An upper-air cyclonic circulation lay over North Interior Karnataka, with a trough extending from the Comorin area towards it across Tamil Nadu and South Interior Karnataka.
Another trough extended from West Bengal to Madhya Maharashtra, passing across Jharkhand; interior Odisha; Chhattisgarh; Vidarbha; and Marathwada.
Together, these features are helping reorganise the piloting wind and rainfall pattern over the South Peninsula.
